card: Optimizes BIP-352 silent payment public key extraction by replacing script evaluation and Solver inspection with direct template matching for P2SH-P2WPKH inputs. Non-segwit P2SH inputs are ineligible for BIP-352 but previously had their full scriptSigs evaluated up to MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE before being rejected. By requiring the scriptSig to be a single push of a 22-byte witness v0 keyhash script, non-segwit P2SH inputs like multisig are rejected about 12x faster in microbenchmarks without running EvalScript. An error in matching could cause silent payment wallets to miss eligible inputs and fail to detect incoming transactions.
changed_since_previous: Switched from checking the witness stack before evaluating scriptSigs to entirely dropping `EvalScript` and `Solver` in favor of directly template-matching the required P2SH-P2WPKH single-push scriptSig format.
evidence: PR benchmarks show non-segwit P2SH multisig inputs are ruled out about 12x faster (from 688.30 ns/input down to 56.87 ns/input), and P2SH-P2WPKH evaluation saves roughly 200 ns per input (from 7,158.19 ns to 6,949.45 ns).
problem: When extracting public keys from inputs for silent payments, `GetPubKeyFromInput` evaluated every P2SH scriptSig with `EvalScript` and then ran `Solver` on the redeem script, even though only P2SH-P2WPKH is eligible. Evaluating full scriptSigs wastes CPU time on non-segwit P2SH spends like multisig, whose scriptSigs can reach `MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE`.

risk.why: A flaw in scriptSig template matching could cause silent payment scanners to misidentify or miss valid P2SH-P2WPKH inputs, failing to detect incoming wallet funds.

summary: Replaces script evaluation and Solver inspection in BIP-352 input public key extraction with direct template matching for P2SH-P2WPKH inputs. A new helper, `CScript::IsPayToWitnessPubKeyHash()`, checks whether a script is a 22-byte witness v0 keyhash program, allowing `GetPubKeyFromInput` to verify P2SH-P2WPKH scriptSigs without running `EvalScript`.
